disclaimer.metaDescription: Important information about the educational nature of this website, the off-label use of ketamine, and the limits of what's offered here.
disclaimer.heading: Disclaimer
disclaimer.reviewNote: This disclaimer should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel before the site goes live.

sections.heading: Educational information only
paragraphs: The content on this website is provided for general educational purposes only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment, and it is not a substitute for the guidance of a qualified health provider. Never disregard professional medical advice, or delay seeking it, because of something you have read here.

sections.heading: Off-label use
paragraphs: Ketamine is FDA-approved as an anesthetic. Its use for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and other mental health conditions is "off-label." Off-label prescribing is legal and common when supported by sound medical evidence, but it means these uses have not been formally approved by the FDA for that purpose.

sections.heading: No guarantee of outcome
paragraphs: Ketamine-assisted therapy is a relatively new and still developing intervention. While research is encouraging, individual results vary and no specific outcome is promised or guaranteed. Benefits are generally most durable as part of an overall treatment program.

sections.heading: No therapeutic relationship
paragraphs: Using this website or contacting us through it does not create a therapist–client or provider–patient relationship. Any such relationship begins only after a formal consultation, assessment, and agreement to treatment.

sections.heading: Not a crisis service
paragraphs: This website and its contact form are not monitored around the clock and are not a crisis or emergency service. If you are in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 (U.S.), or dial 911 for emergencies.

sections.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: This website collects only the information you choose to submit through the consultation request form — your name, email address, optional phone number, and message. We ask that you do not include sensitive health information in that form.

sections.heading: How we use it
paragraphs: We use the information you provide solely to respond to your inquiry and, if appropriate, to schedule a consultation. We do not sell your information or share it with third parties for marketing.

sections.heading: Form processing
paragraphs: Form submissions are processed by our hosting provider (Netlify) and delivered to us by email. Their handling of submitted data is governed by their own privacy practices.

sections.heading: Health information
paragraphs: Any protected health information gathered as part of actual treatment is handled separately, under the confidentiality protections that apply to medical and therapy records — not through this website.

sections.heading: Your choices
paragraphs: You may request that we delete the information you submitted through this site at any time by contacting us at the email address on our contact page.

informedConsent.metaDescription: Key information about ketamine-assisted therapy — its benefits, risks, side effects, eligibility, alternatives, and the voluntary nature of participation.
informedConsent.heading: Informed Consent & Beyond
informedConsent.intro: This summary covers important information about ketamine-assisted therapy and about the medicine itself. Please read it carefully and bring any questions to your consultation.
informedConsent.callout: This page is educational. Before beginning treatment, you'll review and sign a complete informed-consent document with Becky, and you'll have the chance to ask anything you wish. It's very important to us that you feel safe and respected throughout.
informedConsent.reviewNote: A complete, signed consent document is provided during intake. This summary should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel before launch.

sections.heading: Why the medicine is paired with therapy
paragraphs: Ketamine may be most effective when paired with therapy. It doesn't cure on its own; rather, it creates an altered, open state that supports change. Preparation, guidance during the session, and integration afterward are what help turn a powerful experience into lasting growth. Your active engagement shapes the results.

sections.heading: Benefits
paragraphs: Many people experience improvement in mood and a reduction in symptoms such as depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic manifestations. Ketamine is distinguished by its rapid onset, and the research indicates a roughly 70% initial response rate. Durable improvement usually requires more than one session and is most robust as part of an overall treatment program. Results are not guaranteed.

sections.heading: Potential risks & side effects
paragraphs: Ketamine has an extensive safety record, but as with any medicine there are potential risks. The most common physical effect is a short-term rise in blood pressure, pulse, or heart rate, which can matter for those with heart disease. Other possible effects include dizziness, lightheadedness or sedation; impaired balance, coordination or slurred speech; temporary confusion or altered perception; nausea or vomiting; and headache or anxiety.

These effects are transient and generally resolve within about four hours. Repeated, high-dose, non-medical use of ketamine has been linked to urinary and bladder problems; this is much less likely under medically-supervised treatment. Ketamine can also worsen certain conditions in people with psychotic, severe personality, or dissociative disorders.

sections.heading: Managing adverse effects
paragraphs: To reduce nausea, avoid eating or drinking for four hours before your session. Resting still with your eyes closed or an eye mask helps with balance and comfort. Your vitals are monitored throughout. We reserve the right to activate emergency response (such as calling 911) if clinical judgment indicates you need a higher level of care.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Before participating, you'll be carefully interviewed to determine whether ketamine treatment is appropriate. You're required to be under the care of a primary care physician and a mental health provider. Some medical and psychiatric conditions must be treated first, and some make treatment inadvisable.

sections.heading: Potential for abuse & dependence
paragraphs: Addiction resulting from medically-supervised ketamine treatment is exceedingly rare, but non-medical use and addiction do occur. Because ketamine can affect mood, thinking, and perception in ways some find compelling, it should only be used under the direct supervision of a licensed prescriber.

sections.heading: Alternatives
paragraphs: No other medicine produces ketamine's specific effect. Psychotherapy without ketamine is available and can be effective. Depression, PTSD, and bipolar disorders are commonly treated with antidepressants, mood stabilizers, and psychotherapy; PTSD is often treated with EMDR; and ECT and TMS are used for treatment-resistant depression.

sections.heading: Confidentiality
paragraphs: Your privacy and all therapy records are kept confidential and maintained with the same precautions as ordinary medical records. Allowing anyone else access to your records requires your signed release.

sections.heading: Voluntary participation
paragraphs: Ketamine is a newer psychiatric treatment, and your decision to undertake it is completely voluntary. Even after agreeing to begin, you may withdraw from treatment at any time.
